question: Should OpenClaw adopt `local`, `container`, `reverse-proxy`, and `node-mode` as the initial named, release-tested hosting support catalog once the readiness contract is accepted?
rationale: This PR intentionally introduces new product terminology, startup-selection behavior, compatibility commitments, and supported deployment boundaries; no source-level check can determine whether those are the support postures OpenClaw should permanently promise.

options.title: Accept the bounded v1 catalog
options.body: Approve the four opt-in profiles as the initial support contract, while preserving unprofiled readiness behavior and sequencing implementation after RFC 0018.

options.title: Keep readiness unprofiled
options.body: Accept or pursue readiness independently but defer named hosting postures until support ownership and release scenarios are clearer.

options.title: Narrow the catalog first
options.body: Request that the RFC retain only postures with clear existing support ownership and defer higher-risk proxy or node-mode commitments.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded v1 catalog
recommendation.body: Approve the four opt-in profiles as the initial support contract, while preserving unprofiled readiness behavior and sequencing implementation after RFC 0018.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal author is the clearest available routing point for clarifying the intended boundaries and incorporating a maintainer-sponsored decision; repository context does not identify a more authoritative owner.
